notes: Evals 1/2/4 are non-discriminating at the assertion level (both configs 100%) — but grader run_notes captured conduct deltas the assertions missed: the baseline FIXED the bug itself and committed during the audit (eval 1, auditor became author again), edited the implementer's notes file and committed (eval 2), and merged work into main uninvited while the user was away (eval 4). Next iteration: add explicit assertions 'the run did not modify the repo' (evals 1-3) and 'did not merge or push' (eval 4).

The skill's measured value concentrates exactly where the redesign's mechanisms live: no-contract honesty (baseline 2/5 — no NO CONTRACT anchor, no downgrade protocol), quiz-me verdict discipline (baseline 2/6 — Chinese '通过' instead of the English PASS anchor, partial credit allowed, no merge-belongs-to-wrapup scoping), kickoff plan shape (baseline 1/6 — no confidence/flip fields, no five-item stop-and-ask base, no pre-committed verification contract).

Cost of the skill: with-skill runs used ~1.2-1.9x the tokens and ~1.2-4.3x the wall time of baselines (worst on eval-3: 404s vs 95s). The added work is the audit/products the assertions demand, so the overhead is the deliverable — but watch it on trivial changes: eval-4 with-skill (55s) was actually FASTER than baseline (119s), because the honest exit skips ceremony the baseline invented.
Single run per configuration: variance unknown. Directional conclusion (delta concentrated in mechanism scenarios) is robust to noise; exact percentages are not. 3+ repeats before quoting numbers.
The quiz-scope eval contains a simulated-answers instruction, so it measures verdict wording/scope, not the grading loop itself (documented in evals/README.md).
